page: Microsoft Azure D16nds_v6 is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance is provisioned without discrete GPU accelerators.

A key feature of the Dndv6 series configuration is its storage layout. The D16nds_v6 includes a dedicated 945 GB local NVMe SSD for high-throughput, low-latency temporary data operations, while also maintaining compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for persistent managed disks. The instance incorporates network optimization enhancements, though it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, bundling 945 GB of direct NVMe storage provides high-density I/O scratch capability without the operational overhead and provisioning expenses associated with separate attached volumes. However, architectural tradeoffs include the ephemeral behavior of the local NVMe media, requiring persistent state to be offloaded to external disks, and the lack of acceleration hardware for machine learning workloads.

With its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, high networking throughput, and fast local NVMe storage, the D16nds_v6 is suited for database servers requiring high-speed temporary tables and buffer pools, in-memory caching tiers, microservices backends, and continuous integration or build servers.
description: Microsoft Azure D16nds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the network-optimized Dndv6 series, running on an x86_64 Intel processor under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD and support for Premium Storage, while omitting discrete GPU accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The integrated NVMe drive enhances cost efficiency for temporary caching, indexing, and scratch space without incurring extra storage provision fees, though data retention requires external persistent disks. With robust networking and solid-state local storage, the D16nds_v6 is well-suited for database engines with heavy temporary I/O requirements, scalable web serving, cache clusters, and general enterprise application hosting.
